thread:
sam: quick question — we're getting asked by a couple of customers about read-only 'telemetry views' per-customer for debugging (they want to query spans/metrics without touching the raw tenant bucket). Can we do this without exploding storage/ingest costs?

maria: do you mean materialized views or an API-backed read proxy that filters on namespace?

sam: materialized views would be ideal (faster queries, RBAC friendly). concern is duplication + extra retention tiers.

josh: fwiw we already push per-tenant export streams to S3/archives. Idea: materialize a lightweight read index with only span headers + selected attributes (no full payload) and shorter retention. That reduces cost and PII risk.

alyssa: +1 on attribute filtering. We need policy around what is allowed in the view. Otherwise customers might request sensitive attrs like cookie/session ids.

sam: exactly. UX question: in console should this be an opt-in per-tenant toggle (disable by default), or opt-out? Legal probably wants explicit consent.

maria: legal wants explicit opt-in for anything that widens access. So opt-in. But we also need an admin API to grant view access to a given customer-team and to mask attributes.

josh: technical sketch: collector/exporter produces tenant namespaces as normal, then a streaming job fans out to a "view" store. Pseudocode:```yaml
# pseudo otel-collector pipeline
receivers:
  otlp:
exporters:
  s3/archiver:
  view-streamer:
processors:
  filter/attributes:
    include: ["traceid", "spanname", "duration_ms"]
    mask: ["user.email"]
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [filter/attributes]
      exporters: [s3/archiver, view-streamer]
```

josh: the view-streamer writes per-customer read shards (clickhouse or pre-aggregated parquet) and sets an RBAC tag for console to honor.

alyssa: operational concerns: doubling exporters + extra downstream processing increases our bursty CPU footprint. Need autoscale + backpressure. Also query isolation — we must rate-limit read views per customer to protect our analytics cluster.

maria: console UX: show "Telemetry Read View" toggle in tenant settings. If enabled, show a short retention label (e.g., 7d / 30d) and a sanitized fields list. Admins can request longer retention via support.

sam: one more: how do we handle rollbacks when a view accidentally includes a sensitive attr? We won't be able to delete data from downstream analytic stores instantly. Need a mitigations checklist.

alyssa: mitigation ideas: 1) conservative default filters; 2) ability to rotate encryption keys for view store (so data becomes unreadable); 3) purge job for recent partitions and a legal escalation flow. All reasonable?

josh: rotation helps but doesn't work for third-party analytic stores. For those, we'd recommend keeping view-store in our managed lake or Clickhouse we control. If customer requires external export, require DPA + extra controls.

observability-bot: note: "view-streamer" job currently has 75% CPU headroom in staging, but spikes at 2x during load tests.

maria: next steps: (1) draft a minimal privacy-safe schema for views (sam/josh), (2) prototype view-store using parquet + partitioned S3 + Athena for interactive queries (alyssa to validate cost/scale), (3) console toggle mock (maria/devex).

sam: i'll take the schema draft. tagging @maria @josh for follow-up. thanks folks :thumbsup:

josh: also let's add quota enforcement: view-query QPS per-tenant + global throttles. We don't want heavy queries hitting the view-store and hurting other customers.

alyssa: adding rate-limit + cost-metering events so we can correlate view-queries to customer's bill.

maria: I'll schedule a quick sync later this week to align on policy and UX.

sam: done — thanks everyone.
